Hi John —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Attached is the latest order form with our proposed commercial redlines (Proposed_OrderForm_redline_v3.docx). Before we send legal a formal redline pass, can you confirm two items from procurement to avoid back-and-forth: 

1) Invoicing cadence: do you want monthly invoices or quarterly invoicing for consumption over the committed baseline?
2) Net terms: I see "Net 45" in your template notes. Is that a hard requirement for ACME or is Net 30/45 flexible depending on billing cadence?
3) Taxes / evidence: please provide a tax residency certificate or VAT registration so we can populate tax handling and withholding clauses correctly.
4) PO timing: will ACME raise a PO prior to provisioning or after the first invoice? If PO before provisioning, we can queue provisioning once we receive the PO and initial invoice payment (see suggestion below).

Suggested path: we can accept Net 45 if ACME can remit an advance invoice equal to 25% of the first-year commit before provisioning. That covers initial risk and lets finance proceed. If ACME needs split invoicing by legal entity or region, flag that now.

I copied Ben (finance/sales ops) and Marissa (legal) to coordinate redlines and evidence. When you share the certificate and PO template, Ben will confirm invoice remit details and Karthik (cc'd on follow-ups) will confirm any tax withholding obligations on our side.

Thanks for following up. A few quick answers: 

- Invoicing cadence: Procurement prefers quarterly invoices consolidated per legal entity; however, we can accept monthly if Redwood requires it. Please advise which is operationally easier for you.
- Net terms: ACME standard is Net 45; procurement will push for Net 60 only in rare circumstances. Net 45 is fine.
- Tax evidence: attaching ACME_Tax_Residency_Certificate.pdf and our PO template (ACME_PO_template.docx). The certificate should satisfy the standard withholdings; check with your tax/finance.
- PO timing: Procurement will issue a PO once the order form is signed; it typically arrives 3-5 business days after countersignature. For expedited provisioning we can issue a provisional PO earlier if that helps.

Attachment: ACME_Tax_Residency_Certificate.pdf; ACME_PO_template.docx

All —

Reviewed quickly. Guidance below and next steps: 

1) Tax evidence: ACME_Tax_Residency_Certificate.pdf looks standard; sufficient for our cross-border withholding paperwork. Karthik, confirm the country-of-residence field aligns with the W-8/W-9 flow.

2) Net terms: Net 45 is acceptable. Keep Net 45 in the order form. Do not accept Net 60 without executive approval.

3) Advance invoice: I support the 25% advance invoice for initial provisioning. Add a sentence to the order form that provisioning is contingent on receipt of the initial invoice payment (not simply PO). That protects us operationally.

4) PO vs Order Form: ACME PO template is standard. We can accept a PO post-countersign, but if ACME can issue a provisional PO earlier, accept and proceed on receipt of the provisional PO + initial invoice payment. 

5) Redline edits: I made a few targeted edits and added a brief tax allocation paragraph and a payment fallback clause (if an invoice is disputed >30 days, charges remain due but subject to credit notes after investigation). See attached: Proposed_OrderForm_redline_v4.docx. I also created a DocuSign envelope and placed the order form there to streamline signatures: https://www.docusign.net/ej-sign/abc123-orderform

Next steps: Naomi — send v4 to John with the suggested invoice schedule and request provisional PO/initial payment instructions. Ben / Karthik — confirm invoice dates and remit address; I will stand by for legal countersign if any further edits are requested.
